{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABi9P1vw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhMTbZw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 156, "title": "Make save-state selection, Save and Load available in gameplay fullscreen", "body": "## Problem

The player provides a unified save-state selector and explicit Save and Load actions, but these controls and their picker are outside the fullscreen gameplay container. Players must exit fullscreen every time they want to save, restore or choose a state. This interrupts gameplay, especially on phones.

The sibling nes-rust-neo player already supports save management in fullscreen. Adopt the same shared-controls approach for WonderSwan, without bringing unrelated player controls or native-save profile management into fullscreen.

## Expected outcome

- In both desktop and touch fullscreen, the existing save-state selector, Save and Load actions are directly available in a compact management area alongside the fullscreen exit control.
- The same selected state, history, picker and event handlers are used in windowed and fullscreen play. Selecting a state or New state alone does not save or load. Save creates or overwrites the selected target; Load restores it without leaving fullscreen.
- The existing picker supports New state, selection, Delete, Import and Export from fullscreen, subject to browser-imposed native file-dialog limitations.
- Save/load feedback is visible without shifting the gameplay picture or touch buttons during ordinary use, or intercepting gameplay input. Actionable errors remain readable.
- Keep the fullscreen experience focused on gameplay: picture, eleven touch buttons where appropriate, compact save-state controls and exit. Do not add Reset, Pause, cartridge/model settings, ordinary player toolbar, or native-save profiles to fullscreen. Preserve the recently introduced icons and direct-load behavior without automatic backup.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: [376cbb5](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/376cbb573bdea35561b6f898f7ca1f0886f8af7b), after #154 / #155. Inspect latest main before implementation.

- [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): the existing .state-controls group (#select-state, #save-state, #load-state) is in the header; #state-picker and #state-status are outside #game. The fullscreen container contains .fullscreen-viewport, .fullscreen-layout, picture, touch controller and #exit-fullscreen.
- [web/src/main.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): statePicker initialization, canFocusGame(), fullscreenchange, playerChrome inert handling, Escape and fullscreen exit/focus restoration. The current modal-race handling exits fullscreen when a modal opens during entry; distinguish the supported state picker from unrelated Help/cartridge dialogs.
- [web/src/state-picker.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/state-picker.ts): reuse existing selection, busy state, picker, feedback and save/load handlers.
- [web/src/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): existing responsive fullscreen layout, state-controls, state-status, dialog and safe-area rules.
- Reference: [nes-rust-neo #11 / #12](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/pull/12), at [5a579dc](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/commit/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403), particularly [web/src/main.js](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403/web/src/main.js), [web/src/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403/web/src/index.html) and [web/src/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/5a579dc84c52559298a69511b6c1f6d62d40b403/web/src/style.css). It moves the existing state-controls group on fullscreenchange and shares its dialog and selection. Its stable save-feedback approach is also relevant. Do not copy NES/FDS-specific controls, save profiles or recovery logic.
- Related WonderSwan work: #146 / #147 (gameplay fullscreen), #150 / #151 (unified save-state management), #152 / #153 (remove automatic recovery), #154 / #155 (mute and fullscreen icons).

Reproduce using an original CC0 fixture: insert a ROM, enter fullscreen and attempt to choose a save state or save/load. Today the existing controls are unavailable in fullscreen.

### Implementation scope

- Prefer moving the single existing state-controls DOM group between its normal header position and a compact fullscreen management region, as in nes-rust-neo. Make the existing state picker and status feedback available within the fullscreen presentation through shared elements (for example, place the dialog within #game and move/reposition the feedback as appropriate). Do not duplicate IDs, handlers, dialogs, selection or persistence state. Keep the shared elements accessible rather than inert while fullscreen is active; keep unrelated application chrome inert.
- In fullscreen, group the state selector, Save, Load and compact exit icon together, preferably above gameplay, away from the hardware input buttons. Provide the controls for desktop as well as touch users. Preserve Escape/native exit and a discoverable fullscreen exit. Keep the selected destination recognizable, using truncation for long names where needed. Preserve semantic button names, disabled/busy states and keyboard navigation.
- Keep eleven game controls at least 44×44 CSS pixels, the correct orientation-specific arrangement, picture aspect ratio, safe-area handling, and non-overlapping management/gameplay hit regions. Use a simple bounded layout with scrolling at constrained sizes when needed. A compact management row may consume some display space; do not attempt to maximize every pixel or require a simultaneous no-scroll fit in arbitrary extreme viewports.
- Open and dismiss the shared picker without exiting fullscreen. Preserve modal focus and input isolation, including Escape dismissing the picker rather than unnecessarily exiting fullscreen; native browser exit behavior is acceptable. Return focus appropriately after selection, save/load, cancellation, or fullscreen exit. If the browser exits fullscreen while a dialog or native file picker is open, the operation remains coherent in windowed mode, without stale inert elements or lost selection. Do not force re-entry or introduce a browser-specific workaround for unsupported native picker behavior.
- Save and Load retain existing running/paused intent, snapshot validation, RTC rebase, audio/input clearing and captured-frame restoration. Fullscreen entry/exit does not mutate selected state or restart the machine. Preserve ROM/model scoping, explicit New state creation and selected-state overwrite. No automatic state creation, recovery backups, new storage schema, snapshot format changes or Rust core changes.
- Keep transient feedback from shifting or intercepting the picture and touch controls (e.g. a bounded non-interactive status overlay or an existing fixed feedback region). Keep save/load errors readable and avoid layout jumps when messages appear/disappear. Focus on the actual usability issue, not exact geometry for every text length and viewport. Keep normal player behavior and styling consistent.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Using real Wasm and an existing CC0 fixture, enter native fullscreen and choose New state, Save, overwrite the selected state, choose another existing state and Load. Verify correct guest restoration, unchanged selection on entry/exit, and no unwanted history entries or automatic backup. Exercise the same state from the windowed player. Verify that the actual fullscreen target remains the gameplay container.
- [ ] The shared picker opens, selects and dismisses in fullscreen with working keyboard and touch focus, no click-through or unintended gameplay input, and usable Delete/Import/Export actions. Exercise representative cancellation and native exit while a picker is open; document browser-imposed native file-dialog limitations. Reuse existing save-state coverage rather than retesting the entire storage failure matrix in fullscreen.
- [ ] Verify a representative desktop viewport and the bounded mobile matrix of 375×812 and 812×375, with 320×568 as a constrained case, using both horizontal and vertical game presentations as applicable. The picture, eleven gameplay controls, save-state controls and exit remain reachable, with non-overlapping hit regions and existing minimum touch sizes. Scrolling is acceptable for constrained space. Verify save/load feedback does not move gameplay targets or prevent input during ordinary play. No exhaustive breakpoint sweeps or new extreme safe-area permutations.
- [ ] Preserve existing fullscreen entry/exit, focus, orientation, display, mute, visibility suspension/resume and manual save-state behavior. Briefly update README/Help to describe fullscreen state controls.
- [ ] Run applicable existing production-preview checks: npm ci, npm run build:wasm if needed, npm run build, npm run test:browser, npm run test:compat, and git diff --check. Reuse existing builds and focused coverage. No Rust or fixture changes/checks are needed for a frontend-only change. Record actual results and limitations.

### Completion and scope discipline

This is a focused UI integration, not a new save system or fullscreen redesign. Review against the stated goals and bounded viewport matrix. Only material supported-use defects (incorrect state restore, data loss, inaccessible essential controls, accidental destructive actions, broken input or required test failure) block merge. Minor visual polish, hypothetical storage races, arbitrary adjacent-pixel viewport changes and additional screenshots do not. Do not expand the acceptance matrix or require repeated full-suite runs on unchanged revisions. No human approval, commercial ROM or physical phone is required. Once the requested workflow works, mandatory tests pass and no material regression remains, approve, merge and close.

## Optional validation

A representative fullscreen screenshot or mobile WebKit smoke check if useful. Neither is required.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge and closure, verify the Pages deployment of the merge revision and briefly smoke-test the published player with an original CC0 fixture: enter fullscreen, select/create a state, save, overwrite, load and exit, confirming the same history in windowed mode. Record the workflow URL, actual observations and limitations.
